title: Observability forwarder v2: polyglot exporter refactor, zero-copy ring buffer & async encoder
creator: Anika Shah
description: Replace the legacy observability ingestion path with a modular, low-contention forwarder (v2) that supports multiple exporter protocols (OTLP/gRPC, OTLP/HTTP, custom UDP for legacy infra). The goal is to reduce p50/p99 export latency under peak load, cut CPU and allocation overhead in the runtime, and make it easy to add new exporter adapters without touching hot-path code. This ticket tackles engineering debt related to global statics, coarse locks, and the synchronous encoder that amplify tail latencies.
background: Over the last 18 months we've added exporter-specific hacks into the forwarder: per-exporter goroutine pools, duplicated batching logic, and a synchronous protobuf encoder that allocates heavily and blocks request threads during export spikes. Production incidents (2025-11-12 and 2026-01-21) showed export stalls when a downstream tracing backend experienced backpressure; these stalls propagated and increased request tail latency. Previous tickets (ENG-49217, ENG-44122) reduced some allocation hotspots but the core forwarder remains brittle and hard to extend.
proposed_solution: 1) Introduce a zero-copy ring buffer for span/metric/log records between the runtime producers and the exporter workers. 2) Move encoding to a dedicated async encoder pool that supports pluggable encoders (protobuf, json, custom compact binary). 3) Implement per-tenant adaptive batching with budgeted flush timers to respect latency SLOs. 4) Add a protocol adapter layer to support OTLP/gRPC and OTLP/HTTP with backpressure-aware gRPC flow control. 5) Replace global mutable statics with per-shard state to remove the global lock. 6) Add a lightweight delta-counter pre-aggregator for high-cardinality counters to reduce cardinality and per-export size.
tasks: Design ring buffer API and shard mapping (proto + design doc)
Implement zero-copy producer API in runtime hot path
Build async encoder pool with pluggable encoder interface
Create exporter adapter interface and implement OTLP/gRPC + OTLP/HTTP adapters
Add per-tenant adaptive batcher and flush budget controller
Benchmark end-to-end under synthetic high-QPS traces and real workload replay
Add e2e tests and integration tests for backpressure and failover
Rollout canary on internal staging with telemetry gating
Document migration path and deprecation notes for old forwarder
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end export p99 latency for traces reduces by >= 35% under representative peak workload
CPU allocation from tracing/metrics/logging path drops by >= 40% in microbenchmarks
No increase in request tail latency (observed in consumer SLO dashboards) during canary rollout
Forwarder supports OTLP/gRPC and OTLP/HTTP with transparent failover between them
New forwarder has test coverage for adapter failures and backpressure scenarios
Migration doc published and runtime flag exists to enable v2 forwarder per deployment
implementation_notes:
- Language: Go (match runtime). Keep zero-copy semantics via pooled byte buffers and slice headers; avoid reflection in encoder hot paths.
- Use sharded ring buffers keyed by tenant shard to reduce cross-tenant contention.
- Encoder pool should be sized conservatively and backpressure signals propagated to ring buffer producers.
- Provide compatibility layer so existing consumer code sees same Record struct; adapters translate to exporter wire formats.
- Add metrics: forwarder_buffer_size, encoder_pool_active, exporter_backpressure_duration, batch_flush_ms.
- Plan for gradual rollout: feature flag + per-cluster opt-in.
tests_and_validation:
- Microbenchmarks comparing old vs new exporter pipeline using benchtool (trace-generator) covering: small spans (8-64B), medium spans (256-1KB), and high-cardinality counters.
- Integration tests: simulate exporter latency, gRPC stream resets, and intermittent HTTP 503s. Verify that producer threads are not blocked >200ms.
- Load test in staging with replication of 2x production QPS for 4 hours and monitoring for OOM/GC spikes.
- Validate telemetry dashboards and SLO alerts remain green during canary.
rollback_plan:
- Keep previous forwarder implementation packaged and toggled by runtime feature flag.
- Canary rollout in two waves: internal -> staging -> production. If p99 request latency worsens by >10% or exporter error rate increases above threshold, flip feature flag.
- If rollback required, coordinate with infra and alert on exporter errors and backlog growth to avoid silent data loss.
